identity.title: LER 2022-001-00 for Susquehanna Steam Electric Station, Unit 2 re Inadequate Performance of Loss of Safety Determination Resulting in Both Divisions of Core Spray Being Inoperable

cause.proximate_text: The cause of the event was determined to be inadequate performance of a loss of safety function determination by the Operator. The review failed to identify a loss of safety function resulting from concurrent inoperability of both divisions of Core Spray, Division 1 of Core Spray for planned maintenance and Division 2 of Core Spray due to performance of a surveillance. This cause was attributed to human performance.

nodes.display_name: Division 1 Core Spray out of service for planned maintenance
nodes.description: LCO 3.5.1 Condition A entered to support planned maintenance on Unit 2, Division 1 Core Spray beginning 09/25/2022 ~19:45.

nodes.display_name: Loss-of-safety-function determination performed with outdated procedure copy
nodes.description: Operations used a previously completed copy of the station procedure, which did not identify the Unit 2, Division 1 Core Spray ongoing planned maintenance.

nodes.display_name: Missing required peer check for LCO entry
nodes.description: A peer check for entry into LCO 3.7.2 Condition C was not received as required by station procedures.

nodes.display_name: ESW Division 2 stroke-time surveillance rendered Division 2 Core Spray inoperable
nodes.description: Performance of the quarterly stroke time testing of ESW to TBCCW/RBCCW isolation valves results in inoperability of Unit 2, Division 2 Core Spray.

nodes.display_name: Both divisions of Core Spray inoperable / loss of safety function
Revoked licensed operator qualifications pending remediation
Perform focused observations of loss of safety function determinations

chain: inadequate loss-of-safety-function determination [cause TBD/human performance] -> stale procedure copy used, missed Div 1 Core Spray maintenance -> missing required peer check for LCO 3.7.2 entry (concurrent with ESW surveillance disabling Div 2 Core Spray) -> both divisions of Core Spray inoperable, loss of safety function (~9 min) [no backup asserted; engineering analysis found Div 2 Core Spray could still have performed its function]
notes: Cause code TBD/provisional per FORM-366 fields; category left as 'provisional' per instructions even though narrative attributes cause to human performance. No component failure occurred (component failure info: not applicable); this is a procedural/human-performance event. No previous occurrences reported, so no SIMILAR_TO edge or stub LER created. ESW surveillance and Division 1 planned maintenance are treated as two parallel failure-mode branches converging on the missing-peer-check step, which is the proximate trigger for the loss of safety function; the origin of the causal chain (stale procedure use) is linked CAUSED_BY to the Cause node per the human-performance determination. No BACKED_UP_BY edge asserted since no system was stated as an operable backup during the 9-minute window — engineering analysis after the fact found Division 2 Core Spray could have functioned, but this is an analysis conclusion, not a stated-operable backup during the event.
